Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder. President Trump is back in Washington, D.C. arriving at

with polls showing a tight race against Democrat James Tallarico. Trump's remarks were interrupted

and its latest advisory, the National Hurricane Center in Miami, says that storm has strengthened
into a category one hurricane with top sustained winds of 75 miles per hour, and it's on track
toward the Gulf Coast for later this week. The storm expected to bring heavy rain and the potential
for flash flooding. The State Department says it has officially requested additional information
from Russia about the death of a lab worker amid fears of pneumatic plague, but President Trump is
downplaying concerns about how this could be linked to a bioweapons program, as in Pierce
Michelle Kellerman reports. President Trump says the Russians have given "a little information"
about the situation in Irkutsk. He was asked whether this could have been the result of work
on a bioweapon. Well, we don't think so. We're going to find out soon enough, but we don't think so.
And if you listen to them, it's under control. Russia's public health agency says the lab worker
died of pneumonia, and that it was not related to her work at the Anti-Plague Research Institute
in Irkutsk. Michelle Kellerman, NPR News, the State Department. Coronel's student group staged

Kennedy Young is a junior at Cornell studying public policy. She's the co-president of Black

sit with and discuss with. The issues that she dealt with are the incident that occurred to her,
but here we are sitting with each other for seven hours in community. She says one of the group's
demands is changes to Cornell's policy to set minimum sanctions for perpetrators of sexual
assault on campus. For NPR News in Ithaca, I'm Phoebe Taylor Vuello. This is NPR.
The state of Texas has carried out the first execution since Christa Pike's failed lethal
injection in Tennessee. 46-year-old Jamal Howard was pronounced dead Wednesday evening after
receiving the same drug. Howard's attorneys unsuccessfully sought to block the injection,
arguing that he was intellectually disabled and faced similar risks as Pike. Pike's attorneys say
she is now aware of what happened and is angry and confused. On Wednesday, a judge said she would
issue an order to the state to preserve evidence in the case. The World Wildlife Fund has published
its Biennial Living Planet Report, which chronicles a 73 percent drop in the average size of monitored
wildlife populations from 1970 until 2022. Here's NPR's Ari Daniel. This year's index adds almost 300
species, and the overall global decline in biodiversity doesn't appear to be slowing down.
But the report points to a handful of species that have recovered or ticked upwards due to
sustained conservation efforts—bluefin tuna, green sea turtles, tigers, and certain populations
of elephants. Rebecca Shaw is WWF's chief scientist. This gives us hints into how we should be doing
conservation overall to reduce the systems that drive the degradation of nature. The report says,
quote, "collective hope is the most reliable predictor we have of whether large-scale change
will occur." Ari Daniel, NPR News. Nation shares declining in Thursday trading, the regional markets

topics.text: President Trump rallies Texas voters behind Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton in San Antonio
First Atlantic hurricane of season strengthens to Category 1, threatens Gulf Coast this week
State Department requests information from Russia about lab worker death amid pneumonic plague fears
Cornell student groups stage seven-hour sit-in protesting university's handling of alleged sexual assault
Texas executes 46-year-old Jamal Howard using same lethal injection drug that failed in Tennessee
World Wildlife Fund reports 73 percent decline in monitored wildlife populations since 1970
